entry_state: Policy transfer needs feasible actions and information, not just an adapted learned process. Off-policy states and multiple equilibria limit conclusions from residuals. Validation therefore separates implementation, model coherence and empirical adequacy, then challenges evidence admission, hidden history, state memory, information timing, scenario meaning and financing cash conventions.
exit_state: Validation follows complete transactions and retained unknowns, including terminal liabilities and cross-module changes. A small synthetic company now supplies opening accounts, observed profit and gross cash flows, one compatible event history and balanced journal bundles. Its closing reports still do not identify customer concentration or fixed-versus-floating debt.

observations.finding: Balanced journals can use the wrong recognition or reporting mapping. Aggregation tests must compare joint paths and adaptive decisions, while terminal comparisons retain outstanding obligations. Complete cross-module event sequences test shared identities, dates and units.
observations.disposition: retain; no inference from aggregate balance or isolated module tests to correct composition

observations.finding: The reference ladder separates exact finite semantics, numerical approximation and forecast validation. Failure regions remain visible; no probability renormalization after computational failures is permitted. The chapter clearly limits its examples to exact/analytic diagnostics.
observations.disposition: retain method scope; source support for scoring rules remains inherited pending its own review

observations.finding: The small-company opening has assets 200 and debt/payables/equity 100+40+60=200. Reported profit is 120-70-25-5-10=10; exclusions include tax, dividends, acquisitions and OCI.
observations.disposition: retain explicit synthetic scope; not a whole real-company acceptance case

observations.finding: The event witness gives receivables20, inventory40, payables50, property90, cash70 and equity70; closing assets220 equal liabilities/equity220. Journal descriptions distinguish accrual from cash settlement and capital cost from depreciation.
observations.disposition: retain checked arithmetic; one witness does not identify actual customer or debt composition
